description: Computer Science student from Multan, Pakistan, taking on NASA Space Apps 2026 as a solo team. My project, VITA, helps flight surgeons keep astronauts healthy on long missions with live vital-sign monitoring, early warnings and smart alerts. I enjoy software engineering, data visualization and turning ideas into working products. Team is complete, but feel free to reach out to share ideas. Let's go beyond orbit!
summary:
VITA is a crew health mission-control platform that lets a flight surgeon see the health of every astronaut in one place, in real time. It streams vital signs (heart rate, blood oxygen, blood pressure, respiration and body temperature), checks each reading against clinical thresholds, and raises alerts that escalate automatically if nobody acknowledges them. Trend analysis gives an early warning before a value becomes critical.

The design follows NASA's five hazards of human spaceflight. VITA tracks radiation dose rate and each astronaut's mission dose against the 600 mSv career limit. It also monitors sleep and wellness for isolation and confinement, shows the signal delay to Earth for distance (1.3 s from the Moon, up to 22 minutes from Mars), and watches cabin air quality for the hostile closed environment. Missions can be scoped to LEO, the Moon or Mars.

With one click, VITA turns live data into professional PDF medical reports and Excel workbooks.

This matters because crews going beyond Earth orbit cannot rely on instant help from the ground. VITA turns raw telemetry into clear, early, actionable health decisions. It is built with .NET 10, PostgreSQL, SignalR and Next.js.
details:
WHAT IT DOES

VITA (Vital Integrated Telemetry for Astronauts) is a crew health mission-control platform. It gives a flight surgeon one real-time view of every astronaut's health. Vital signs stream in live: heart rate, blood pressure, blood oxygen, body temperature, respiration and radiation dose rate. Each reading is checked against its clinical safe range. When a value goes outside its range, VITA raises an alert. If nobody acknowledges the alert, it escalates automatically: critical alerts after 2 minutes, warnings after 15.

An early warning score adapted from NEWS2 combines all vitals into a single risk number. Trend analysis projects when a value will cross its limit, for example "heart rate projected to cross 50 bpm in about 45 minutes", so the team can act before an emergency.

VITA is organised around NASA's five hazards of human spaceflight:

- Radiation: daily dose rate, and each astronaut's mission dose against the 600 mSv career limit.

- Isolation and confinement: sleep, mood and stress from daily wellness check-ins.

- Distance from Earth: the live signal delay (1.3 s for the Moon, 3 to 22 minutes for Mars).

- Gravity fields: the mission day and the gravity environment.

- Hostile, closed environment: cabin CO2, O2, pressure, temperature and humidity.

Missions can be scoped to low Earth orbit, the Moon or Mars. With one click, the live data becomes a professional PDF medical report with charts, or an Excel workbook containing every reading.

BENEFITS AND INTENDED IMPACT

Beyond Earth orbit, a crew cannot rely on instant help from the ground. VITA turns raw telemetry into clear and early decisions. It reduces information overload by staying calm by default: colour appears only for clinical state, and the screen becomes loud only when something needs attention. Reports make every decision documented and easy to share. The long-term goal is a tool that also supports the crew itself when the signal delay makes ground support too slow.

TOOLS AND TECHNOLOGIES

- Backend: C# and .NET 10 with Clean Architecture (Domain, Application, Infrastructure, API) and ASP.NET Core minimal APIs, with rate limiting and output caching.

- Data: PostgreSQL with Entity Framework Core migrations.

- Real time: SignalR pushes vitals, cabin readings and alerts to every screen.

- Frontend: TypeScript, Next.js 16, React 19, TanStack Query and Tailwind CSS, with light and dark themes and a command palette.

- Reports: QuestPDF for the PDF reports and ClosedXML for the Excel workbooks.

- Quality: 95 automated xUnit tests, plus a telemetry simulator that generates realistic crew data for demos.

No special hardware is needed. The data source is designed so that real wearable sensors can replace the simulator.

WHAT MAKES IT CREATIVE

Most health dashboards show numbers. VITA is built around the hazards that are specific to spaceflight, so radiation budget, signal delay, isolation and cabin air appear next to the vitals. It predicts problems instead of only reporting them, and it treats calm design as a safety feature.

FACTORS CONSIDERED

- Alarm fatigue, which is why alerts escalate in levels.

- Signal delay on deep-space missions.

- Readability under stress: one accent colour, and status colours used only for clinical state.

- Clinical safe ranges taken from published guidelines.

- Performance and reliability: live updates, caching, and loading states.

- Accessibility: keyboard navigation, contrast, and light and dark themes.

- Honesty: VITA is a decision-support prototype, not a certified medical device.

AI ASSISTANCE

I developed VITA as a solo developer. AI tools (Claude) assisted with parts of the code, UI design, documentation and these texts. All architecture decisions, review, testing and integration were done by me.
